Q: Adjust ttk.Treeview column width to fit its contents and make horizontal scrolling viable A:

It's possible to calculate the width of each individual item in the treeview column and therefore determine the width required for the column to not cut off its content:

def ttk_text_width(text, _widget={}):
    if not _widget:
        _widget["window"] = tk.Toplevel()
        _widget["window"].withdraw()
        _widget["window"].update()
        _widget["label"] = tk.ttk.Label(_widget["window"])
        _widget["label"].pack()
    _widget["label"].config(text=text)
    # TODO Apply font settings, like font size or family
    _widget["label"].update()
    return _widget["label"].winfo_width()

def max_item_width(treeview, item=None, indent=None, depth=1, focus_open=False):
    if indent is None:
        # TODO For Tcl/Tk 9.0 or later, indent is available as widget option, see https://www.tcl-lang.org/man/tcl9.0/TkCmd/ttk_treeview.html#M107
        indent = 20  # Default value for earlier versions
    width = 0
    for item in treeview.get_children(item):
        image_width = 0  # TODO If item has an image, add its width
        width = max(width, ttk_text_width(treeview.item(item, "text")) + image_width + indent * depth)
        if treeview.item(item, "open") or (focus_open and item == treeview.focus()):
            width = max(width, max_item_width(treeview, item, indent, depth + 1, focus_open))
    return width

def update_column_width(treeview, *args, **kwargs):
    treeview.column("#0", stretch=False, width=max_item_width(treeview, *args, **kwargs))

treeview.bind("<<TreeviewOpen>>", lambda event: update_column_width(event.widget, focus_open=True))
treeview.bind("<<TreeviewClose>>", lambda event: update_column_width(event.widget))

update_column_width(treeview)

Function update_column_width needs to be called every time the treeview contents change.

There's two events <<TreeviewOpen>> and <<TreeviewClose>> to update the treeview when an item has been opened or closed (i.e. we do or don't have to consider the widths of its child items for the column width). However, <<TreeviewOpen>> needs a little bit of extra work, because the event triggers "just before setting the focus item to -open true", so treeview.item(item, "open") would still return False:

<<TreeviewOpen>> Generated just before setting the focus item to -open true. <<TreeviewClose>> Generated just after setting the focus item to -open false.

Source: https://www.tcl-lang.org/man/tcl9.0/TkCmd/ttk_treeview.html#M103

Q: As a beginner I struggle with floating point numbers A:

But yes, I basically agree with the others. When asking questions, and especially when you are a working professional, you should aim for a more expansive explanation of what a problem or concern is. Your colleagues will not appreciate you making them do all the work to help you with your issues.

Please explain:

  • What is "the print line", what do you mean, and where is that in the code?

  • Why does the exercise become how to convert a double to an integer? What actually is the problem, what is the desired result, how did you conclude that converting to an integer was necessary?

Q: How do I make git commit -a not add submodule changes? A:

Run this command i the main repo:

git config submodule.<name>.ignore all

It will make Git completely ignore the submodule's state during git status and git commit -a.

number 2:

You can automate a check that stops developers from committing an outdated submodule pointer if they forgot to update it.

Create or edit .git/hooks/pre-commit in the main repo:

#!/bin/sh
# Check if any submodule is un-synchronized with the index
if ! git diff --cached --submodule=short | grep -q '^+++ b/'; then
    # If the user is trying to commit an old pointer, warn them
    if git diff --submodule=short | grep -q 'submodule changed'; then
        echo "ERROR: Your submodule pointer is out of date."
        echo "Please run 'git submodule update' before committing."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

It blocks the commit entirely if the submodule is dirty.
